comparison.stem:
A 503A pharmacy receives a bulk ingredient with a certificate of analysis, but the container states 'research use only' and 'not for human use.' Staff plan to use it in a patient prescription because its assay result is within specification.

Which assessment is appropriate? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Confirm ingredient eligibility; the assay and COA alone are insufficient.
A shorter BUD changes the ingredient to a human-use grade.
Patient consent substitutes for the ingredient requirements.
The COA permits use if the pharmacist doubles the final quality checks.

comparison.stem:
A Schedule II prescription is faxed for a resident of a qualifying long-term-care facility. The pharmacy has verified the required prescriber and patient information; other applicable requirements are satisfied.

What is the federal effect of the LTCF fax exception? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The fax is valid only as a follow-up to a previous emergency dispensing.
The fax permits release only if an emergency oral order is also obtained.
Treat this qualifying LTCF fax as the original, subject to the other requirements.
The fax permits preparation, but a paper original is required before release.

comparison.stem:
A licensed, noncertified technician is approved to receive unchanged verbal refill authorizations. A caller instead changes a patient's directions from one tablet daily to two tablets daily.

What is the appropriate next step? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Ask the pharmacist to assess the new directions before recording authorization.
Accept the change because the ingredient and tablet strength remain unchanged.
Accept the change after confirming that insurance will pay for the larger quantity.
Record an unchanged refill and attach the new directions as a counseling note.

comparison.stem:
A hospital purchaser sees a supplier on FDA's outsourcing-facility list. The supplier advertises every compounded preparation it sells as 'FDA approved because this facility is registered.'

Which correction is most accurate? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Each preparation is FDA approved once the facility reports that product.
The facility is registered; individual preparations are not thereby FDA approved.
Only the preparations shipped for office use are automatically approved.
The facility registration operates as a separate ANDA for every formulation.

comparison.stem:
A pharmacist is checking patient-information requirements for three services: a refill of a drug requiring a Medication Guide, a dispensed oral-contraceptive package, and a routine vaccine for which a VIS is required.

Which actions match the document to the service? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Treat provision of these documents as a substitute for assessing counseling needs.
Supply the required Medication Guide with the qualifying refill.
Provide the VIS before the vaccination.
Provide the applicable oral-contraceptive patient package insert with the package.
Replace all three documents with the same software-generated CMI sheet.

comparison.stem:
An authorized collector has removed and sealed an inner liner under the required procedures. A staff member proposes reopening it to count each patient's tablets so the pharmacy can improve its inventory detail.

Which handling approach is appropriate? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Keep the liner sealed and document its required identifiers.
Remove usable tablets for the pharmacy's return-to-stock bin.
Sort the contents by patient before resealing the same liner.
Open the liner under a single technician's supervision.

comparison.stem:
An outgoing and incoming MOR prepare an ordinary change-of-MOR inventory. The pharmacy holds oxycodone, clonazepam, pregabalin, and PMP-reportable gabapentin.

Which inventory scope is appropriate? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Include oxycodone alone because the pharmacy maintains a perpetual CII record.
Include the federally scheduled products but omit gabapentin as nonfederal.
Count the federally scheduled stock and the PMP-reportable gabapentin.
Include oxycodone and clonazepam but omit lower schedules.

comparison.stem:
A pharmacy's original controlled prescription contains the prescriber's DEA number. During label review, a technician assumes that every field on the original prescription must appear identically on the patient's container.

Which distinction should the pharmacist explain? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Information present in the original prescription need not be accurate on the label.
A correctly printed container label eliminates the need to retain the prescription.
Check the separate original-prescription, dispensing-record and label requirements.
The pharmacy can remove patient directions if the prescriber gives written instructions elsewhere.

comparison.stem:
A pharmacist is reviewing incoming prescriptions in Massachusetts. Any electronic-prescribing exception mentioned below is valid; it does not waive other controlled-drug requirements. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A practitioner replaces the actual issue date with a future date so that a later fill appears to be newly issued.
A pharmacist verifies a duplicate-looking EPCS and replacement paper order before any second dispensing.
A pharmacy treats a valid paper-format exception as permission to omit the remaining controlled-prescription requirements.
An authorized agent independently selects a different drug and dose while transmitting the practitioner’s order.
A pharmacist treats a successful insurance adjudication as resolving credible prescription-forgery concerns.

comparison.stem:
An adult asks for a patient-specific emergency-contraception prescription for a friend under the Massachusetts statewide standing-order pathway. The pharmacist has not spoken with the person who will use the medicine.

Which next step fits that pathway? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Use the purchaser's history as the intended patient's screening record.
Generate the prescription under the purchaser's name and change it after pickup.
Contact and assess the intended patient, using an allowed phone or in-person route.
Require the intended patient to be physically present even if a telephone assessment is available.

comparison.stem:
A licensed intern under direct pharmacist supervision has entered a new prescription, completed preparation, and counseled the patient. The pharmacist has not performed final dispensing verification.

What must occur before the prescription is released? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The intern may substitute a second barcode scan for pharmacist verification.
Another intern may independently verify the first intern's work.
Have the pharmacist perform final dispensing verification before release.
The pharmacist may postpone verification until the end-of-day reconciliation.

comparison.stem:
For a vaccine requiring a VIS, the pharmacy prepares to give the patient a VIS link on the receipt after the injection. The patient has not received the VIS in any other form.

Which change is needed? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Replace the VIS with the pharmacy's privacy notice before the injection.
Give the link with the post-injection receipt because the lot is documented.
Make the appropriate VIS available to the patient before this injection.
Provide the VIS only if the patient later reports an adverse event.

comparison.stem:
A prescriber's assistant enters the practitioner's selected drug and directions into a prescription system for the practitioner to review and sign.

Which actions stay within the agent distinction? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Transmit an already authorized order through a pathway that permits agent communication.
Choose a different controlled drug based on the assistant's own assessment.
Use the practitioner's credentials to sign an EPCS without the practitioner's authorized signing process.
Provide the practitioner's emergency oral CII authorization in place of the practitioner.
Prepare the prescription information for the practitioner's authorized signature.

comparison.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacy reviews clozapine dispensing on October 26, 2026. A pharmacist proposes ignoring a patient-specific neutropenia concern because there is no REMS clearance step.

Which overall conclusion correctly addresses the current regulatory and safety obligations? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Treat removal of the REMS as removal of the need for ANC monitoring and clinical safety review.
Dispense only after restoring the former REMS enrollment and authorization process.
Apply the isotretinoin iPLEDGE dispensing window as the replacement clozapine rule.
Remove the former REMS access requirement, while retaining appropriate label-based monitoring and patient-specific review.

comparison.stem:
A pharmacy sent its required dispensing file to the PMP system. A staff member says this transmission also proves that the pharmacist reviewed the patient's controlled-substance history before dispensing.

Which explanation is accurate? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A clinical query eliminates the pharmacy's future reporting obligation.
A successful upload automatically documents every pharmacist's clinical query.
Any employee with reporting access may inspect any patient's history for personal interest.
Data submission and patient-specific clinical review are different functions.

comparison.stem:
A 503A pharmacy receives a bulk ingredient with a certificate of analysis, but the container states 'research use only' and 'not for human use.' Staff plan to use it in a patient prescription because its assay result is within specification.

Which assessment is appropriate? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Confirm ingredient eligibility; the assay and COA alone are insufficient.
A shorter BUD changes the ingredient to a human-use grade.
Patient consent substitutes for the ingredient requirements.
The COA permits use if the pharmacist doubles the final quality checks.

comparison.stem:
A 503A pharmacy receives a bulk ingredient with a certificate of analysis, but the container states 'research use only' and 'not for human use.' Staff plan to use it in a patient prescription because its assay result is within specification.

Which assessment is appropriate? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Confirm ingredient eligibility; the assay and COA alone are insufficient.
A shorter BUD changes the ingredient to a human-use grade.
Patient consent substitutes for the ingredient requirements.
The COA permits use if the pharmacist doubles the final quality checks.

comparison.stem:
A supervising physician refers an adult patient for retail CDTM. The pharmacist has the referral and the original consent remains in the physician's record. The physician asks when the consent copy must be sent to the pharmacist.

Which deadline applies to this communication? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Within 48 hours.
Within 7 calendar days.
Within 72 hours.
Within 24 hours.

comparison.stem:
A newly hired staff pharmacist is asked to execute a paper Form 222 for the pharmacy. The pharmacist did not sign the registrant's registration application and has not received a power of attorney.

What is missing from the proposed signing arrangement? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A supervisor's later countersignature substitutes for the required authority.
The employee's pharmacist license automatically supplies ordering authority.
The supplier's willingness to accept the signature establishes its validity.
An applicable signing authorization, such as a properly executed power of attorney.

comparison.stem:
The pharmacy is using the non-vaccine medication-administration pathway in DCP 26-03-124. Personnel, patient, product, and prescription requirements are otherwise met. An administration-related event leads to inpatient hospitalization.

Which response accurately reflects the circular’s wording? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Follow the prescriber’s appropriate reassessment interval; quarterly is an example rather than a universal fixed deadline.
Appropriately communicate the reaction to the prescriber within 24 hours as the circular recommends.
Immediately report the event to the prescriber; assess any separate Board reporting duties.
Use professional judgment and contact the prescriber as encouraged to clarify the intended administration setting.

comparison.stem:
A licensed intern under direct pharmacist supervision has entered a new prescription, completed preparation, and counseled the patient. The pharmacist has not performed final dispensing verification.

What must occur before the prescription is released? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The intern may substitute a second barcode scan for pharmacist verification.
Another intern may independently verify the first intern's work.
Have the pharmacist perform final dispensing verification before release.
The pharmacist may postpone verification until the end-of-day reconciliation.

comparison.stem:
A pharmacy asks the Board to waive a facility requirement. The request remains pending, and no emergency authorization has been issued.

Which action is appropriate while the request is considered? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Treat the owner's professional license as interim waiver authority.
Apply the requested waiver to related federal requirements as well.
Implement the proposed alternative on the date the request is submitted.
Follow the existing requirement until the applicable waiver is granted.

comparison.stem:
A supervising physician sends the sole original signed CDTM consent to the community pharmacist and keeps only a chart entry stating that consent was obtained. There is no retained electronic copy. The patient has copies of the referral and consent. The pharmacist is organizing the program's permanent records.

Which record arrangement should the pharmacist coordinate with the physician? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Keep the original at the pharmacy and let the physician's chart notation stand in for the consent.
Let the patient keep the only signed document because both professionals recorded the referral.
Have the physician retain the original and remove the pharmacy's consent record after confirmation.
Return the original to the physician and retain pharmacy copies of the referral and consent.

comparison.stem:
Under a retail CDTM protocol, a pharmacist discontinues a medication because of an urgent safety concern. The physician's office is closed, but the agreement specifies an urgent communication channel and a covering physician. The pharmacist has documented the action in the patient's medical record.

What is the appropriate next communication step? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Send the change in the next routine batch because the patient record has already been updated.
Wait until the office opens because the supervising physician personally must receive the first notice.
Send only the routine copy within 24 hours because that deadline applies to every circumstance.
Use the agreement's urgent coverage procedure now and transmit the discontinuation information.

comparison.stem:
A pharmacy is revising a CDTM agreement that says only, "Support staff may assist the pharmacist." The program uses interns and technicians for permitted support tasks. The pharmacist must replace the vague sentence with terms that comply with the CDTM delegation requirements.

Which provisions belong in the agreement? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Identify the pharmacist duties that may be delegated and those that must remain with the pharmacist.
Authorize technicians to resolve clinical therapy conflicts if the pharmacist reviews the decisions later.
Specify when and how delegation occurs and the duration of the delegation.
Use the weekly staffing roster in place of terms identifying which duties may be delegated.
Define the scope of delegated work within the applicable intern and technician rules.

comparison.stem:
A certified pharmacy receives a valid Sublocade order. The patient asks to collect the depot syringe and take it to the clinician later. The staff is familiar with handing buprenorphine/naloxone films directly to patients.

Which supply distinction should guide the pharmacist? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Convert the depot order into films using the same total milligrams.
Use ordinary take-home pickup because both products contain buprenorphine.
Remove the REMS restriction by placing a 'professional administration only' label on the bag.
Use the depot's applicable healthcare-provider delivery pathway.

comparison.stem:
A customer selects an FDA-approved OTC naloxone product and pays without requesting prescription insurance billing. The cashier says a patient-specific prescription is required because the pharmacy also uses a statewide standing order.

Which distinction should the pharmacist explain? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: OTC purchase and prescription billing are separate pathways.
The statewide order converts the OTC product into a prescription-only product.
Any OTC naloxone purchaser must enroll in an opioid-treatment program.
Cash payment permits dispensing any prescription-only overdose-reversal product without an order.

comparison.stem:
A retail pharmacy sends prescription processing to an authorized central-fill pharmacy. The patient will collect the finished prescription at the retail pharmacy. A manager calls this a patient-requested refill transfer and closes the retail record without preserving the shared-service linkage.

Which correction is appropriate? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Keep the retail/central-fill roles linked in the required shared-service records.
Keep only the shipping label because the finished product returns to retail.
Restart the prescription's validity period when central fill receives it.
Treat the central-fill pharmacy as the patient's prescriber.

comparison.stem:
A customer selects an FDA-approved OTC naloxone product and pays without requesting prescription insurance billing. The cashier says a patient-specific prescription is required because the pharmacy also uses a statewide standing order.

Which distinction should the pharmacist explain? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: OTC purchase and prescription billing are separate pathways.
The statewide order converts the OTC product into a prescription-only product.
Any OTC naloxone purchaser must enroll in an opioid-treatment program.
Cash payment permits dispensing any prescription-only overdose-reversal product without an order.

comparison.stem:
A pharmacist practices CDTM throughout the year and has completed the usual 20-hour general CE requirement. The record contains no additional CDTM-related education.

What education remains under the stated CDTM CE structure? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Five additional approved hours related to the CDTM practice area.
Five hours selected from the same 20 already used to meet the general minimum.
No additional hours until the two-year agreement renewal.
Five additional hours for every prescription changed under the agreement.

comparison.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacy creates a rule that treats every PMP-reportable drug as federal Schedule V. It applies that rule to gabapentin and pregabalin.

Which correction is appropriate? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Remove gabapentin from PMP reporting because it is not federally scheduled.
Move pregabalin to Schedule VI because both drugs treat neurologic conditions.
Distinguish federal scheduling from gabapentin's state reporting status.
Apply CII no-refill rules to both because their dispensing is reported.

comparison.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacy is offered manufacturer samples labeled 'not for resale.' It plans to remove that wording, repackage the samples, and sell them as ordinary prescription stock.

What is the principal problem? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Samples may be sold if their expiration date is more than a year away.
Repackaging eliminates the need to retain the original product identity.
Samples become regular inventory once an insurer accepts their NDC.
Removing sample wording does not authorize the planned resale and repackaging.

comparison.stem:
A Massachusetts patient lawfully receives a requested partial fill of a CII prescription. Before receiving the remainder, the patient asks for transfer to a different pharmacy under the initial-unfilled-EPCS rule.

Which fact defeats that proposed route? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Some of the prescription has already been dispensed.
The patient has fewer than five refills remaining.
The request came from the patient rather than the insurer.
The second pharmacy carries a different generic manufacturer.

comparison.stem:
For a vaccine requiring a VIS, the pharmacy prepares to give the patient a VIS link on the receipt after the injection. The patient has not received the VIS in any other form.

Which change is needed? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Replace the VIS with the pharmacy's privacy notice before the injection.
Give the link with the post-injection receipt because the lot is documented.
Make the appropriate VIS available to the patient before this injection.
Provide the VIS only if the patient later reports an adverse event.

comparison.stem:
A pharmacy keeps expired controlled-substance stock in a secured quarantine area while arranging lawful disposition. Staff propose excluding it from the on-hand inventory because it is no longer available for dispensing.

What is the appropriate inventory treatment? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Exclude it when the product expiration date passes.
Include the secured stock in the applicable on-hand accounting.
Count only the portion expected to generate a financial credit.
Exclude it as soon as a reverse-distribution pickup is requested.

comparison.stem:
The compliance calendar has a row for a Massachusetts nonresident Drug Store pharmacy license. The manager must use that license’s ordinary expiration cycle, not the renewal date of another credential.

Which calendar entry matches this credential? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: December 31 of the even-numbered renewal year
December 31 every year
December 31 of the odd-numbered renewal year
The licensee’s birthdate in its two-year renewal cycle

comparison.stem:
The MOR is away for three days and has designated the pharmacist on duty to cover inventory adjustments. Two Massachusetts-licensed technicians with current national certification conduct the CII perpetual-inventory count for oxycodone tablets under written procedures. The team finds that a receipt was entered twice, and the pharmacist confirms the cause from the source records.

Which steps fit the permitted workflow? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Accept the two technicians’ signatures as a substitute for pharmacist verification of the completed count.
Have the supervising pharmacist verify that the count was completed in accordance with Board requirements.
Let either technician correct the balance using the authority to enter CII receipt transactions.
Treat the MOR’s return as a prerequisite for any discrepancy adjustment.
Have the pharmacist designee make the discrepancy adjustment and report the change to the MOR.

comparison.stem:
For the relevant calendar year, a dispensing practitioner has dispensed 6,000 controlled-substance dosage units and distributed 250 units counted under the limited distribution exception. A proposed stock transaction would distribute 200 additional units. All units use the same proper counting basis; assume no other transactions or exceptions.

What does the dosage-unit percentage calculation show after the proposed transaction? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The denominator excludes all distributed dosage units.
The proposed proportion exceeds 5%; do not rely on this limited distribution exception.
Only the dollar value of the proposed transfer determines the 5% test.
The proposed annual dosage-unit proportion does not exceed 5%; other conditions still must be satisfied.

comparison.stem:
A registered pharmacy first engages in its controlled-substance business activity before its first stock shipment arrives. It has no controlled substances on hand at that start point.

How should the initial inventory requirement be handled? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Use the first supplier invoice as a substitute for the initial inventory.
Wait until the first biennial inventory is due.
Postpone the initial inventory until the second shipment.
Record the absence of stock as the initial inventory.

comparison.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacy reconciles its CII perpetual records with physical quantities every 10 days. Its previous federal biennial inventory was more than two years ago. The MOR says the frequent CII reconciliations eliminate the separate federal inventory duty.

Which response is correct? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Perform the separate federal inventory without extending its two-year interval.
The pharmacy may inventory only its CII stock to cure the federal omission.
A biennial inventory is needed only if a CII discrepancy is found.
The frequent reconciliation extends the federal interval to three years.
